_comment: Test corpus for the typed-search query parser (program plan D1).
Each case is a query a sommelier could plausibly type into the palette,
with the parse it must produce. The corpus is the acceptance bar: a
parser change that breaks a case here is a regression in what the search
box understands, and adding a capability means adding cases FIRST.
Fields omitted from `expect` default to empty. `text` is the residue
handed to trigram/ILIKE matching after extraction — the part of the
query that names a wine rather than describing one. Note that the parser
never judges whether a residue word is a real producer: 'chateau' and
'zzqqxx' are both just words to it, and only the search itself can say

cases.why: the plain case — nothing to extract, everything is the needle
a vintage is a filter, and must leave the needle
vintage first reads the same as vintage last
two years named means both are wanted, not a range collapse
a bottle size is not a vintage — 1500ml must not become a year
a country name is a filter and leaves the needle
the demonym means the same country as the noun (the D1 gap)
a demonym with an irregular stem, beside a two-word region — both are recognised, so nothing is left to search as text
a grape is not in the gazetteer and must survive as the needle — the parser narrows the search, it does not swallow it
two countries are two filters — country is a list, not a winner
a multi-word country matches as one span, not two tokens
a region is a filter of its own, and implies nothing about its country
multi-word regions match as one span
region and country together, both kept
colour is a filter — asking for red excludes white, it does not merely prefer it
a structural quality is a PREFERENCE — it ranks, it must never exclude
a pairing word is not a search filter — it stays in the needle and misses, which is what routes the user to the companion
everything at once, in the order a person types it
a word the parser cannot place stays in the needle for the search to judge
connective words are neither needle nor unmatched noise
accents and case fold — a French speaker's spelling still matches
an empty query parses to nothing at all rather than throwing
